Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rewrite the above formula as

$$
2\operatorname{cos}⁡6x=2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x).
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(3x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(3x)+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡6x+{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡6x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+4x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )+\frac{(\pi /2)^{3}}{3}+4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}]-[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}+4\cdot 0] \\  & =[0+\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}+2\pi ]-0 \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{24}+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
